title: CGPA and UK Degree Equivalence: Check Your University's Requirements
seoTitle: CGPA to UK Degree Equivalence: What to Check
seoDescription: Understand UK degree equivalence without a misleading CGPA formula. Prepare grading evidence and check the destination university's requirements.
intro: There is no universal calculation that converts every CGPA into a UK degree classification. Use the university's country guidance and provide the grading scale from your own institution.
description:
Your CGPA needs its academic context

A CGPA is not a universal unit. A score from one institution cannot be converted into a UK degree class simply by applying a single percentage formula. Universities assess qualifications using their own entry policies and country guidance, often with requirements for particular courses or institutions.

Start with the destination university’s published information for your qualification. Then read the programme entry requirements. If the course asks for a UK 2:1 or equivalent, the equivalence is an admissions assessment, not a conversion you can reliably declare from a generic internet table.

Provide complete grading evidence

Keep your official transcript, qualification certificate and grading scale together. Include the maximum score, pass mark and classification rules where the institution supplies them. If your record reports both a percentage and a CGPA, use the official relationship rather than calculating a new one yourself.

Explain an unusual feature briefly: a changed grading system, transferred credits or a different scale used for part of the degree. Do not edit grades or present an estimated conversion as an official result. Follow the university’s document and translation instructions.

A practical enquiry

A useful message names the course and qualification, then provides the awarding institution, country, overall result and grading scale. Ask whether the qualification meets the published academic requirement or whether the university needs further evidence.

For example: “I am considering [course] for [intake]. My degree from [institution] uses a [scale] grading system, and my final result is [actual result]. Could you point me to the relevant country guidance or advise which documents are needed to assess equivalence?” This is an illustrative template; fill it only with accurate information.

Distinguish eligibility from selection

Meeting the minimum academic requirement does not guarantee admission or funding. A programme may also consider research experience, relevant modules, a proposal or other evidence. A scholarship may set its own threshold. Keep these checks separate so that an acceptable degree is not mistaken for a confirmed award.

If your result is below a stated minimum, check whether the policy permits other qualifications or experience to be considered. Do not assume a strong statement overrides an essential requirement. Ask about an available route before paying for another application or qualification.

Keep a course comparison

For each shortlisted course, record the academic threshold, country guidance, required supporting evidence and separate funding rules. Leave uncertain points marked as questions. This produces a more reliable shortlist than a table claiming that one CGPA always equals one UK classification.

Keep the grading scale with your transcript

Ask your institution for the scale used to award your degree, including the maximum score, pass mark and any classification rules. Send that alongside the official transcript when requested. If your university reports both an overall CGPA and a percentage, use its own official conversion rather than an internet formula. Explain unusual features of the record briefly and accurately. The destination university makes the equivalence decision; your task is to provide complete evidence so that a number is not interpreted without its academic context.

Do not invent a conversion formula

Multiplying a CGPA by a constant may produce a percentage, but it does not establish a UK degree classification. Grading scales, pass marks, institutional practices and qualification structures differ. Use the destination university's published international-qualification guidance and the course's own academic requirement together.

If an application asks for the original result, enter that result accurately. If it asks for a converted value, follow the provided method or ask admissions which evidence to supply. A self-calculated equivalence should not appear on your CV as though it were awarded by either institution.

A document pack for an equivalence enquiry

DocumentWhat it contributes
TranscriptModule results, credits, attempts and the final result.
Award certificateExact qualification title and awarding institution.
Official grading scaleMaximum score, pass mark and classification rules where supplied.
Programme requirementThe UK standard or international threshold the course actually asks for.
Translation, where requiredAn accepted version of documents not in the required language.

Keep scans complete and readable. Do not crop a grading key because it seems unrelated to the overall score. If the qualification includes transferred credits or a changed scale, explain that feature briefly and provide official evidence when requested.

Read country guidance with the course page open

University guidance can distinguish between qualification types, awarding institutions or degree durations. Check that you are reading the entry relevant to your actual award. A threshold for a bachelor's qualification may not answer a question about a master's, and meeting a general equivalent does not establish every subject prerequisite.

For example, Oxford publishes country-specific qualification guidance while also directing applicants to individual course requirements. This is evidence that the university makes a contextual assessment, not a universal conversion service that should be copied into every application.

Can I write UK 2:1 equivalent on my CV?

Only use an equivalence you can justify through the relevant official guidance or assessment, and identify it accurately. Reporting your original qualification and grade is usually clearer than presenting a self-declared classification.

Does meeting the equivalent grade guarantee admission?

No. Minimum academic eligibility and competitive selection are different. A programme may also assess relevant subject preparation, research evidence and other required materials.

Record what an admissions answer actually says

If an office confirms that your qualification can be considered, keep that response with the programme name and intake. Do not turn consideration into a guaranteed offer or apply the answer to a different institution. Ask whether the response concerns the degree level, the overall result or a particular prerequisite. Those are related but distinct checks. If your final result is not yet available, provide your current record accurately and identify the expected award date. Avoid entering an estimated final grade as though it has already been awarded. Update the university through its stated process when the official result becomes available.

Official sources and further reading

Requirements and policies should be checked for your programme and application date. Sources checked on 19 October 2026.

  • Oxford: international qualifications
  • Cambridge: postgraduate entry requirements
